extracted.intended_audience: writers, composition students, and educators (U.S. high school and university level)
extracted.subtask_short: writing style guide (The Elements of Style)
extracted.subtask_description: A concise, prescriptive English usage and composition guide (Strunk's The Elements of Style, 1918 edition) covering elementary rules of usage, principles of composition, matters of form, commonly misused words, and spelling. Useful for students, teachers, and writers seeking succinct, normative guidance on clear English prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary Rules of Usage (Rules 1–8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The original 1918 edition detailed eight elementary rules of usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as concise numbered rules; audio listing separates Rules 1–4 and Rules 5–8. The book frames these as basic, prescriptive prescriptions for correct English usage intended for students and writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary Principles of Composition (ten rules, Rules 9–18)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of elementary principles of composition (the book lists ten such principles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles are given as numbered rules for composing clear prose; the audio tracks break these into multiple segments (Rules 9–10, 11–13, 14–16, 17–18). They serve as prescriptive guidance on organization, emphasis, and expression in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Few Matters of Form
rubrics_metrics.description: A short section covering specific matters of form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The section collects conventional formatting and presentation conventions (punctuation/formatting concerns) as brief prescriptive points. Appears as a distinct section/track in the recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words and Expressions Commonly Misused
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of words and expressions commonly misused (presented as guidance to avoid errors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book compiles commonly 'misused' words and expressions with recommended usage; the audio divides this material across tracks (e.g., 'all right to most' and 'nature to would'). Intended as a practical reference to correct typical usage mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short prescriptive guidance on spelling conventions; appears as a discrete section/track in the edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescriptive approach to grammar and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The work is described as a prescriptive treatment of English grammar and usage and is influential in U.S. composition teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterized as one of the best-known and most influential prescriptive guides, often required reading in U.S. high school and university composition classes. Emphasizes normative 'rules' for clear English prose rather than descriptive linguistics.
